# Reverse Engineering a 27MHz RC Toy Communication Using RTL SDR

In the world of hobbyist electronics and radio communication, few endeavors are as thrilling as reverse engineering. Recently, an enthusiast took on the challenge of controlling a 27MHz radio-controlled fire engine toy from a laptop, utilizing a Software Defined Radio (SDR) known as RTL-SDR. This article delves into their detailed process, showcasing the technical steps and findings along the way.

## Unearthing the Frequency

The journey began with identifying the operating frequency of the toy, which was found to be in the 27MHz range, specifically at 27.1MHz. Using GNU Radio software, the author visualized the RF signals through the RTL-SDR Source and QT GUI Sink blocks. This initial step set the stage for further exploration.

## Decoding the Modulation Scheme

With the frequency pinpointed, the next task was to determine the modulation scheme employed by the toy. Analyzing the RF signal in the time domain revealed that Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK) was the chosen method. To improve the quality of the signal, the author implemented several GNU Radio blocks, including the AM Demod block, Automatic Gain Control (AGC2), and Decimating FIR Filter blocks.

## Visualizing the Output

After demodulating the signal, the author utilized the QT GUI Sink and Audio Sink to visualize the output and even play it back audibly. This hands-on approach not only enhanced understanding but also made the process engaging.

## Analyzing Frame Structures

An essential part of the project was analyzing the frame structure of the communication. By observing sequences and patterns in the time domain, the author estimated frame lengths and employed Symbol Sync and Threshold blocks to represent and count bits accurately.

## Developing a Custom Decoder

To further refine the analysis, a Custom Decode Block was developed to count frame lengths based on identifiable patterns in the data stream. This innovative step showcased the flexibility of using Python within the GNU Radio environment.

## Addressing Buffer Challenges

As with many technical projects, challenges arose. The author faced issues with buffer sizes for longer frames, which were effectively tackled by adding Stream to Vector and Vector to Stream block pairs. This adjustment was crucial in ensuring smooth data processing.

## Results and Insights

Through meticulous analysis, a comprehensive table was created, summarizing the key combinations, frame lengths, data lengths, and data length per 12 bits. Here are some of the findings:

| Key Combination | Frame Length (bits) | Data Length (Frame Length - 12) (bits) | Data Length/12 |
|------------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------|
| ^                | 132                 | 120                                     | 10             |
| V                | 120                 | 108                                     | 9              |
| <                | 24                  | 12                                      | 1              |
| >                | 84                  | 72                                      | 6

# Hacking the Humane AI Pin: A Journey into Discontinued Tech

In a world where technology evolves at breakneck speed, the tale of the Humane AI Pin serves as a fascinating case study of ambition, innovation, and the relentless pursuit of knowledge. When Humane announced the shutdown of its AI Pin services just ten days after selling to HP, few could have imagined that this closure would spark a deep dive into the device's inner workings by a dedicated community of hackers and enthusiasts.

## The Shutdown and Acquisition

On February 18, 2025, Humane made headlines by announcing the impending shutdown of all services for the AI Pin. This decision came swiftly after the company's sale to HP, leaving many tech aficionados disheartened. However, one determined enthusiast seized the opportunity, acquiring two Pins, three boosters, and a charging device for $300 through Reddit. Unfortunately, upon arrival, the devices were rendered nearly useless, stuck on onboarding screens that required server communication that no longer existed.

## Exploring the Depths of the Device

Undeterred, the author turned to leaked APKs—Android application packages that had not been obscured—leading to a collaborative effort among hackers eager to explore the AI Pin's potential. This community-driven initiative unveiled a trove of information, but the most significant breakthrough came when an anonymous tip revealed a private key, granting ADB (Android Debug Bridge) access to one of the Pins.

With this newfound access, the author successfully connected to the device, launching demo apps and exploring its features. However, the journey was far from straightforward; initial attempts to communicate with remote servers were thwarted by SELinux restrictions, presenting a formidable challenge to the budding hacker.

## Discovering Vulnerabilities

As the author probed deeper into the AI Pin's architecture, they identified a vulnerability—CVE-2024-31317—that could potentially grant system permissions. This discovery required extensive research and experimentation, revealing a complex interplay of security measures that initially appeared daunting. Despite the limitations imposed by SELinux policies, the author persevered, seeking a way to communicate with the device while navigating its restrictive permissions.

The journey was not just a technical challenge; it was a lesson in resilience and creativity. The author detailed how to weaponize the identified vulnerability, describing the intricate mechanics of triggering the exploit and overcoming complications arising from the device's setup.

## A Community Effort

The broader conversation around the Humane AI Pin highlighted the collective effort of the tech community. Comments from onlookers expressed admiration for the security measures put in place by Humane, noting that the company's commitment to physical device security was commendable.
